name: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models (Brohan et al., 2023)
observations: Core thesis: a vision-language model (VLM) pretrained on web-scale data can be turned directly into an end-to-end robot policy by expressing robot actions as text tokens, i.e. 'actions as another language'.

Model family is called VLA (vision-language-action). Two instantiations: RT-2-PaLI-X (built on PaLI-X, 5B and 55B) and RT-2-PaLM-E (built on PaLM-E-12B). Largest model used for closed-loop robot control at the time (55B).

Action space: 6-DoF end-effector delta position + delta rotation, plus gripper extension and a discrete 'terminate episode' command. Each continuous dimension is discretized into 256 uniform bins, so one action = 8 integers, serialized as a space-separated string, e.g. '1 128 91 241 5 101 127'.

Tokenization detail: PaLI-X already has a unique token per integer up to 1000, so action bins map to the matching integer token. PaLM-E has no such numeric tokens, so the 256 least-frequently-used tokens are overwritten as the action vocabulary (a form of symbol tuning).
Training data format: standard VQA framing - 'Q: what action should the robot take to [instruction]? A: <action tokens>', images from the robot cameras as visual input.

Key training recipe = CO-FINE-TUNING: mix the original web VLM data (VQA, captioning, WebLI image-text) with robot trajectory data instead of fine-tuning on robot data alone. This prevents forgetting and is what drives generalization. Robot data is upweighted: ~50% of the batch for RT-2-PaLI-X, ~66% for RT-2-PaLM-E.
Ablation result (unseen-condition average): from-scratch 9, robot-only fine-tuning 42-52, co-fine-tuning 44-63; bigger models generalize better. Co-fine-tuning > fine-tuning > training from scratch.

Output constraint: when prompted with a robot task the decoder is restricted to sampling only valid action tokens; on normal vision-language tasks the full natural-language vocabulary is available. No action-specific layers are added - weights are fully shared.

Real-time inference: models are served from a multi-TPU cloud service queried over the network. 55B runs at 1-3 Hz; the 5B variant at ~5 Hz on-robot control loop. Compute cost is flagged as a limitation, with quantization/distillation suggested.

Results over ~6k real-world evaluation trials on a 7DoF mobile manipulator: on par with RT-1 (~91-93%) on seen tasks, but roughly 2x better than the next best baselines (RT-1, MOO) on unseen objects/backgrounds/environments, and >3x better on emergent skills (60% vs 17% for RT-1).

Emergent capabilities inherited from web pretraining (not in robot data): symbol understanding (semantic cues like numbers, icons, logos - 'move apple to 3'), reasoning (math, color matching, multilingual instructions), and person recognition ('move coke can to the person with glasses').

Chain-of-thought variant: augment targets with a natural-language 'Plan:' step before the 'Action:' tokens, e.g. 'Instruction: I'm hungry. Plan: pick rxbar chocolate. Action: 1 128 124 136 121 158 111 255'. Only a few hundred gradient steps needed; enables multi-stage semantic reasoning (pick a rock as an improvised hammer, an energy drink when tired).

Limitations: only semantic/visual concepts transfer - the robot does NOT gain new physical motions, its skills stay inside the robot-data distribution. Weak at part-specific grasps (handles), dexterous/precise motions (folding towels), tool use, and multi-layer indirection. Pushing dynamics of unseen objects fail.

name: LeRobot (Hugging Face)
observations: Context7 ID /huggingface/lerobot, v0.6.1, High reputation, ~4.5k code snippets. Currently the most complete open implementation of the RT-2-style VLA workflow: datasets, training, rollout and hardware I/O in one stack.
Ships VLA policy types usable as direct successors to RT-2's approach: `smolvla` (SmolVLA, small VLM-backed policy), `pi0` / `pi05` (Physical Intelligence VLA policies) and ACT/diffusion baselines.

Training entry point is `lerobot-train`; you point it at a Hub dataset and a base checkpoint, e.g. `--policy.path=lerobot/smolvla_base --dataset.repo_id=${HF_USER}/mydataset --batch_size=64 --steps=20000`. SmolVLA 20k steps is roughly 4h on a single A100.

`--policy.load_vlm_weights=true` is the analogue of RT-2's 'start from VLM pretraining' choice; `--policy.freeze_vision_encoder` / `--policy.train_expert_only` control how much of the VLM backbone is adapted (RT-2 instead shares all weights).

Inference/rollout via `lerobot-rollout` with `--inference.type=rtc` (Real-Time Chunking). RTC exists precisely to solve RT-2's latency problem: large slow VLAs get smooth continuous motion via action chunking with `--inference.rtc.execution_horizon` and `max_guidance_weight` instead of needing a 1-3Hz high-latency cloud call.
Ships simulation eval environments (LIBERO, LIBERO-plus) so a policy can be regression-tested before real-robot deployment; datasets use torchcodec/pyav video backends.

name: Hugging Face Transformers VLM stack
observations: Context7 ID /websites/deepwiki_huggingface_transformers, High reputation. The practical replacement for Google's internal PaLI-X / PaLM-E backbones used in RT-2.

Open VLM backbones relevant to VLA work: PaliGemma (the direct open sibling of RT-2's PaLI-X; single `nn.Linear` `PaliGemmaMultiModalProjector`, dedicated `image_token_id`, `get_placeholder_mask` swaps text embeddings for projected image features) and SmolVLM/Qwen2-VL for smaller on-robot models.

`PaliGemmaProcessor` (a `ProcessorMixin` composing tokenizer + image processor) auto-adds `<image>`/location/segmentation tokens and can generate `labels` automatically by masking prompt tokens via `token_type_ids` - convenient for the RT-2 style 'Q: ... A: <tokens>' supervision format.
`image-text-to-text` pipeline (`ImageTextToTextPipeline`) is the inference path for the VQA half of co-fine-tuning; no default model, must be specified explicitly.
These are the models to co-fine-tune: keep the VLM objective alive while adding the action-token objective, matching RT-2's co-fine-tuning finding that robot-only fine-tuning hurts generalization.

name: VLA action tokenization technique
observations: Reusable design pattern from RT-2: discretize each action dimension into N bins (256 in the paper), map the bins onto tokens that already exist in the backbone's vocabulary (or overwrite the least-frequently-used tokens), and emit the whole action as one short string so a standard next-token-prediction loss covers both language and control.
Termination is encoded as one extra discrete token, letting the policy decide when the episode is done instead of a hand-written heuristic.
Inference must constrain decoding to the action vocabulary for robot prompts, otherwise the model emits invalid tokens; constrain per-prompt, not globally, to keep language ability intact.

Alternative adopted by LeRobot's pi0/SmolVLA lineage: continuous action chunks + flow-matching/action-expert heads, which avoid the discretization ceiling and the 1-3Hz latency of autoregressive token decoding.
